title: Corpus manifest entry
description: One entry describes one rare-but-valid pattern of Stellar ledger data: where its bytes came from, which CAP and protocol made it possible, and what a correct reader must produce from it.

id.description: Stable entry ID: <group>/<slug>. The group is normally cap-NNNN; protocol-gated behaviour without a CAP uses protocol-NN; cross-cutting groups are xdr-strict, strkey, limits.

kind.description: ledger: one full LedgerCloseMeta. xdr: one standalone XDR value. api: an SDK-neutral call with an expected result, no blob. strkey: a text address vector. spec: a contract interface (SEP-48): a Wasm module whose contractspecv0 custom sections hold an SCSpecEntry stream, or a bare SCSpecEntry stream.

caps.description: CAP numbers that introduced or changed this pattern. Empty only for protocol-gated behaviour with no CAP or for pure encoding rules; then 'caps_note' is required.

introduced.description: First protocol version at which stellar-core can emit this pattern.

removed.description: First protocol version at which core can no longer emit it (for example inflation).

synthetic.description: true if the bytes were hand-crafted and stellar-core did not emit them. Bytes imported from core goldens, emitted by a local stellar-core, captured from network history, or sliced contiguously out of such bytes are not synthetic.

negative.description: true if a correct reader must reject this input. Negative entries are always synthetic. For kinds ledger, xdr, spec and strkey it is true exactly when validity is malformed or invalid.

flags.description: Bug classes the input exercises, Wycheproof style; on valid entries too (for example depth at a limit).

shapes.description: Free-form tags for the structural variants this entry exercises.

why.description: Why this pattern trips readers, in one or two sentences.

fields.description: Rows of the guide's field-by-field table (fields.yaml) that this entry demonstrates.

variants.description: The bytes of this pattern on each network. Required for kinds ledger and xdr.

levels.description: Conformance levels that apply. L0 codec round-trip, L1 SDK object parse, L2 decoded values, L3 native conversion, L4 API call.

unit.description: single: served alone at its real sequence. chain: served as part of its scenario run from the first ledger.

chain.description: Scenario run ID when unit is chain.

indexer_scope.description: sdk-only marks entries indexers are not expected to ingest (for example very old protocols).

requires_prior_state.description: true if a reader needs the earlier ledgers of the same chain for this entry to be meaningful (for example a balance update on an existing trustline). Such entries are replayed only as part of their chain.

related.description: Issues, pull requests, CAP sections and advisories this entry relates to.

added_in.description: Corpus version that first shipped this entry.

notes.description: Free-form remarks for reviewers that are not part of any check.

reference.description: What makes the expected value authoritative: bytes or behaviour of the network (stellar-core), a protocol rule (CAP/XDR definition), or a specification (SEP, RFC 4506).

core_behaviour.description: For negative entries: what stellar-core itself does with this input, and how that was established.

mirrors.description: Golden mirror (check AG-4): this entry's focus transaction, replayed on a local stellar-core with the named golden test's own meta flags and setup, has a structural skeleton byte-equal to the golden's focus transaction, with no masks. The mirror run is evidence; the entry's own variants keep their recorded profile.

flags.description: Meta flags the golden's test runs with (those set to true).

flags_source.description: Where in the test source the flags are set (file and lines at the tag).

settings_overrides.description: Network settings copied from the test because they change the meta (for example min_persistent_ttl).

scenario.description: Scenario file and step of the mirror run.

skeleton_sha256.description: Skeleton hash of the golden's focus transaction.

run_skeletons.description: Skeleton hash of the mirror run per network; each must equal skeleton_sha256.

state.description: executed: hashes recorded and equal. planned: declared, not yet run.

allOf.$comment: negative entries are malformed or invalid.
A malformed or invalid entry with bytes or a text vector is negative.
A reject reason that is a rule about decoded values makes the entry invalid.
Every other reject reason is a decoding rule: the entry is malformed.
api: exact or refuse is acceptable; refuse only is malformed or invalid; no refusal is valid.

decimal.description: An integer of any width as a decimal string. Never a JSON number, so 64-bit and wider values survive every JSON parser.

network.description: Passphrase family of the bytes. 'pubnet' and 'testnet' name the passphrase, not the origin: a local standalone chain run on the public passphrase is 'pubnet' with source.kind 'local-core'. 'core-test' is stellar-core's fixed unit-test passphrase. 'none' is for passphrase-independent values.

passphrase.description: Network passphrase the bytes were produced under. 'none' variants (passphrase-independent values such as a bare ScVal) use an empty string.

protocol.description: Protocol version applied when core emitted these bytes.

header_protocol.description: Protocol version in the ledger header, when it differs from the protocol applied (upgrade ledgers).

xdr_type.description: XDR type name as in the pinned stellar-xdr definitions, for example LedgerCloseMeta, TransactionEnvelope, ScVal, LedgerEntry.

validity.description: This variant's validity when it differs from the entry's; absent means the entry's validity.

container.description: spec entries only: how the blob holds the SCSpecEntry stream. wasm: a Wasm module, the stream in its contractspecv0 custom sections; xdr-stream: the bare stream.

framing.description: How the blob holds the value. none: the blob is one value of xdr_type. record-marked: the blob is an RFC 5531 record-marked stream (4-byte marks, as stellar-core writes its meta streams) and the value is record 'frame_index'; every record mark of the stream must be well formed. Only negative xdr entries use record-marked (record-mark error vectors).

frame_index.description: With framing record-marked: the zero-based record that holds the value.

xdr_definitions.description: stellar-xdr tag or commit the type name refers to.

path.description: Path relative to the corpus root. Omitted for bulk-tier entries fetched by hash.

slice_of.description: For an xdr entry cut out of a ledger entry: the parent and where the value sits in it.

path.description: JSON Pointer into the parent's decoded form.

decoded.description: Path to the SEP-51 XDR-JSON rendering produced by the oracle.

decoded_by.description: Oracle library and version that produced 'decoded'.

focus.description: Where in a ledger the pattern is. Lets several entries share one ledger blob.

tx_index.description: Zero-based index into the ledger's transaction processing list (apply order), which is the order of results and meta. It is not the position in the transaction set.

path.description: JSON Pointer into the decoded form.

core_meta_flags.description: stellar-core config flags that affect what meta is emitted.

profile.description: Which stellar-core meta flag set produced these bytes. One ledger has several valid encodings. 'lake' is the flag set Galexie-written public-lake objects have (classic and fee events, ext v1). 'golden-test' is the flag set of one named stellar-core golden test, read from that test's source — there is no single core default, each test sets its own; 'golden_test' must then name the test. 'custom' is any other set, listed in core_meta_flags.

golden_test.description: Required when profile is 'golden-test': the stellar-core test whose meta flags these bytes were produced with.

test_name.description: Human test name from the golden index, without relying on its hash.

flags_source.description: Source file and lines at the tag where the test sets its flags, for example src/transactions/test/InvokeHostFunctionTests.cpp:219-225.

derived.description: Values that depend on the network passphrase or on this particular run. Expectations refer to them as ${derived.<name>}.

tx_hash.description: Hash of the focus transaction on this network.

header.description: Values of this variant's ledger header, as decimal strings, so a shared expectation can pin a header field whose value differs per variant (${derived.header.fee_pool}). Verify checks each against the blob.

contracts.description: Contract addresses that depend on the network ID, by name.

l1.description: Values an SDK's object layer reads from the variant's focus (manifest.md section 10.1), computed by verify with the oracle and compared key for key: a key the focus implies must be present, and no other key may be.

operation_type.description: XDR-JSON snake_case arm of the focus operation's body, for example change_trust.

operation_source.description: The focus operation's own source account as it is on chain (G... or M...).

address.description: The focus operation's counterpart account as it is on chain (G... or M...).

muxed_id.description: Muxed ID of address, else of operation_source, as a decimal string.

decoded_sha256.description: sha256 of the decoded sidecar file, so a tampered or regenerated sidecar is detected.

json_roundtrip.description: A declared exception to the JSON half of the round trip: SEP-51 JSON of these bytes does not reproduce them (for example an empty signed payload). The oracle still requires bytes -> value -> identical bytes and still renders the sidecar; it skips JSON -> bytes, and fails if the JSON round trip in fact succeeds (a stale exception).

requires.description: Mandatory on every variant: the XDR features of the pinned definitions that these bytes use and that older definitions lack, so a reader built on older definitions cannot decode them; [] when none. For a positive variant verify derives the list from the decoded sidecar and requires equality; a negative variant states it by hand ([] unless the defect sits behind such a feature). stellar_value_signed_ms: a StellarValue ext arm with a millisecond close time, signed_ms (arm 3) or empty_tx_set_ms (arm 4) (Protocol 30, CAP-88); sc_address_type_muxed_contract: an SCAddress of type SC_ADDRESS_TYPE_MUXED_CONTRACT (CAP-84).

source.description: Where the bytes came from, with enough detail for a reviewer to obtain the same bytes again.

frame_index.description: Zero-based index of the record-marked LedgerCloseMeta in the file.

test_name.description: Human-readable test name from the golden index.

submission.description: Set when the bytes are stellar-core's answer to a submission rather than ledger output: the refused TransactionResult its /tx endpoint returned for the envelope stored as envelope_entry.

envelope_entry.description: Entry ID of the submitted TransactionEnvelope.

core_role.description: Which stellar-core binary emitted the bytes: the pinned release, a build with test hooks (buildtests), a next-protocol build (vnext), or an old release replaying history (old-core). Absent: release.

scenario.description: Scenario file path relative to the corpus root.

config_sha256.description: Hash of the stellar-core config used.

core_package.description: Official release package the binary came from.

stream_sha256.description: sha256 of the complete record-marked meta stream of the canonical run.

frame_index.description: Zero-based index of this ledger's record in that stream.

generated_by.description: Tool and version that drove stellar-core.

soroban_resources.description: How the Soroban footprint and resource declaration in the envelope were obtained. 'declared' means chosen by the scenario author, not produced by simulation.

inputs.description: Other pinned inputs of the run, for example Soroban settings-upgrade sets.

selected_by.description: Set when the ledger was chosen by a census query rather than by hand: the census file and the query that selected it.

census.description: Path of the census file, relative to the corpus root.

object_sha256.description: Hash of the object as stored (compressed).

batch_index.description: Index of the ledger inside the LedgerCloseMetaBatch.

written_by.description: Core and exporter versions from the object metadata, if present.

refetch.description: Command that fetches the same object.

perishable.description: true if the public source will disappear (testnet resets).

decompressed_sha256.description: sha256 of the object after decompression (the LedgerCloseMetaBatch XDR).

blob_offset.description: Byte offset of this entry's blob inside the decompressed object. The blob is the contiguous XDR encoding of ledgerCloseMetas[batch_index].

object_metadata.description: User metadata of the object exactly as the store returned it.

regenerated.description: true if the lake object was written by a core version newer than the ledger's protocol era (the public lake regenerated old ledgers with current meta).

object_path.description: Path of the vendored original object (.xdr.zst), so the entry can be served byte-identical to the public lake.

recipe.description: How the bytes were built: a base entry plus an edit, or a literal construction.

reason.description: Why stellar-core cannot or would not emit these bytes.

file_kind.description: The archive file the record is cut from: a bucket file or an SCP history file. Absent: bucket.

oneOf.description: Contract code read from a network's ledger: the CONTRACT_CODE entry's code, whose hash is the blob's sha256.

upload_ledger.description: lastModifiedLedgerSeq of the CONTRACT_CODE ledger entry: the ledger that uploaded (or last restored) the code.

fetched_via.description: How the code was read, for example getLedgerEntries on a stellar-rpc.

account.description: An account as a reader should record it: the base account is the identity; a muxed ID is extra routing information, never a different account.

address.description: Base address: G… account, C… contract, B… claimable balance, L… liquidity pool.

on_chain_form.description: The address exactly as its on-chain form renders (M… or W… when muxed).

roles.description: Why the account is a participant. Vocabulary (open; manifest.md section 6.5): source, fee_payer, operation_source, destination, signer_owner, trustline_owner, issuer, counterparty, sponsor, contract, authorizer, liquidity_pool, claimable_balance, claimant. liquidity_pool and claimable_balance mark the L… or B… address of a pool or balance entry that changed; claimant an account named as a claimant of a claimable balance that changed; authorizer an address whose Soroban authorization created a nonce entry (no state change is recorded for nonce entries). counterparty is any other affected address and stays valid for pools and balances.

unverified.description: The author's explicit exception: a stated value the reference extractor cannot derive from the bytes, with the reason. verify's extractor agreement does not require the item; the replay harness scores it not_applicable. It still accounts for the facts it describes under the exactness flags.

expect.description: What a correct reader must produce. Layer 1 is the bytes (variants[].blob). Layer 2 is variants[].decoded. This block is layer 3: semantic facts in a neutral vocabulary, shared by all variants.

reject.description: For negative entries: the input must be rejected.

limits.description: Decode limits the oracle's reject check uses for this entry instead of its own defaults. 'depth' is a nesting depth in stellar-xdr (rs-stellar-xdr) depth units: set it to the boundary the vector is measured against (stellar-core's, converted to these units) so that a vector just beyond that boundary is rejected there and not only at the oracle's provisional default.

values.description: Pinpointed decoded values: a JSON Pointer into the decoded form and the value found there. With 'select', the element of an array of ledger-entry changes, ledger entries or ledger keys is chosen by its ledger key instead of its position (stellar-core writes an operation's change list from an unordered map, so positions differ between runs and passphrases), and 'path' is relative to that element.

path.description: JSON Pointer into the decoded form; with 'select', a JSON Pointer relative to the selected element ('' for the element itself).

select.description: Choose one array element by ledger key. Exactly one element of the array at 'in' must match: a LedgerEntryChange whose entry (or, for 'removed', whose key) has the ledger key 'key' and, when 'change' is given, whose arm is 'change'; a LedgerEntry with that key; or a LedgerKey equal to 'key'. Consumers resolve it per variant to a plain JSON Pointer before comparing; ${derived.*} tokens are allowed in 'in' and 'key'.

in.description: JSON Pointer to the array, for example /v2/tx_processing/0/tx_apply_processing/v4/operations/0/changes.

key.description: SEP-51 JSON of the LedgerKey, for example {"account": {"account_id": "${derived.accounts.A}"}}.

change.description: The LedgerEntryChange arm; needed when the key occurs in more than one change of the array (a 'state' and its 'updated').

events.description: Consensus events (transaction, operation and contract events); diagnostic events are not counted.

result_code.description: Transaction result arm as XDR-JSON names it, for example tx_success, tx_failed, tx_fee_bump_inner_failed.

operation_result_codes.description: One per operation, as <operation>.<code> in XDR-JSON names, for example set_options.success.

participants.description: Who the ledger meta shows was affected. Envelope-only claims are never participants.

exact.description: true if must_include is the complete set.

kind.description: Closed list. Must stay identical to state_changes[].kind in observation.schema.json.

key.description: Canonical strkey of the signer key (G…, T…, X…, P…).

detail.description: Extra facts about the change. The keys allowed for each kind are fixed (see the allOf rules below and manifest.md section 6.6); values are strings (decimal strings for amounts), integers or booleans. A stated key is compared only when the observation carries the same key.

cause.description: What caused the change when it is not the obvious operation, for example 'contract-call' for a trustline created by the Stellar Asset Contract.

tx_index.description: Transaction this fact belongs to (apply order). Defaults to the variant's focus transaction.

only_if.description: Makes the item conditional on a modelling choice the adapter declares in describe (observations.state_changes.modelling). Without the declaration the item is not required, and a reader that reports a matching fact anyway is not penalised. 'initial_authorization_separate': the reader records the authorisation state a trustline is created with as its own change, beside the creation.

unverified.description: The author's explicit exception: a stated value the reference extractor cannot derive from the bytes, with the reason. verify's extractor agreement does not require the item; the replay harness scores it not_applicable. It still accounts for the facts it describes under the exactness flags.

asset.description: native, CODE:ISSUER, or a contract address.

routing.description: The event's to_muxed_id when present. Its type follows what core copied in: a u64 ID, text or 32 bytes. Text and bytes come from memos and are never an address.

count.description: How many records a reader must hold for this movement. Normally 1; pins double-counting bugs.

tx_index.description: Transaction this fact belongs to (apply order). Defaults to the variant's focus transaction.

unverified.description: The author's explicit exception: a stated value the reference extractor cannot derive from the bytes, with the reason. verify's extractor agreement does not require the item; the replay harness scores it not_applicable. It still accounts for the facts it describes under the exactness flags.

addresses.description: Addresses a reader must be able to store and return unchanged.

native.description: Level L3: what a lossless native conversion must preserve.

on_lossy_conversion.description: Acceptable behaviour when the native type cannot hold the value.

error.description: An scvError value: the ScError it holds, as XDR-JSON names (type, for example storage; code, for example exceeded_limit; a contract error's code as its decimal number). The SDK's native value must carry both.

state_changes_exact.description: true if state_changes is the complete set of operation-level state changes of the focus transaction. Scope and exclusions (manifest.md section 6.6): only the focus transaction is looked at; ambient kinds (balance_changed and sequence_bumped, which every transaction causes, and ttl_extended, which the host causes on access) are never counted as extras; an only_if item the reader reports is allowed. Any other state change the reader reports in that scope is a wrong fact.

movements_exact.description: true if movements is the complete set of value movements of the focus transaction, fee and fee_refund excluded (they are matched only when listed and only for readers that model fees). Any other movement the reader reports for that transaction (for example a fabricated or doubled transfer) is a wrong fact.

spec.description: spec entries: the facts the corpus's own section reader reads from the bytes. sections: the number of contractspecv0 custom sections (Wasm only); entries: every whole SCSpecEntry in stream order across all sections, in the neutral rendering of docs/conformance-protocol.md; clean_end: every section decodes to whole entries with no bytes left over.

apiVector.description: An SDK-neutral call. Drivers map 'op' onto their SDK's function.

input.description: Arguments by name. A value that must be passed in a language-native numeric type is written {"native":"number","value":"9007199254740993"}; bytes are {"hex":"…"}; everything else is a string.

expect_reject.description: true if the call must be refused. When expect_reject is true AND expect_xdr_hex or expect_value is also given, either outcome conforms: the exact result, or a refusal ("exact or refuse").

origin.description: For published vectors: the document and vector label, for example SEP-0023 v1.4.0 invalid #15.

knownDivergence.description: A reader known to get this entry wrong in a version range. The conformance runner and harness assert the divergence inside the range and its absence outside it.

target.description: Package or repository, for example @stellar/stellar-sdk, github.com/stellar/go-stellar-sdk, stellar/wallet-backend.

versions.description: Version range. Packages: a semver range. Repositories without tags: a commit range 'A..B' meaning every commit from A to B inclusive on the default branch's first-parent history; '..B' means everything up to and including B.

outcome.description: reject always means a VALID input was rejected; accepts_invalid means an invalid input was accepted.

status.description: 'unreported' is never used in the public manifest for a security-relevant defect; those annotations live in the private overlay until disclosure completes.

observed.description: How we know: executed by us against the named version, read from source, or reported upstream and not re-run.

evidence.description: Path or URL of the transcript or note that shows the divergence.

qualifier.description: For level 'replay': the exact class qualifier the harness must report inside the range.

profile.description: Set when the divergence exists only under a non-default decode profile or sandbox (for example Rust Limits::none()).

finding.description: Finding record ID, when one exists.

match.description: Details the observed cell must also show for the divergence to count as observed, beyond the outcome class. Every field is optional; a stated field must equal the driver's report.

reason.description: The driver's reason code: one of the driver protocol's runResponse.reason.code values (verify checks it against that list).

envelopes_parsed.description: L1 on a ledger: how many envelopes the SDK parsed.

rejected_tx_index.description: L1 on a ledger: an envelope (apply order) that must be among those the SDK rejected.

decimalOrDerived.description: A decimal string, or a ${derived.<path>} token resolved per variant (fees and refunds differ between protocols and networks).

apiOp.description: SDK-neutral operation names for api entries. This named list is the single source; the driver protocol schema references it. Extended only with a schema minor version.

specEntryFact.description: One SCSpecEntry, neutral: kind, name, args ({name, type}) and, for a function, outputs.

validity.description: What a correct reader does with the input (the negative-case vocabulary of the WebAssembly spec tests and Wycheproof). valid: the bytes decode and are accepted (every ledger stellar-core wrote is valid). malformed: the bytes (or text) must fail to decode. invalid: the input decodes, and a validating reader must reject it. acceptable: a reader may accept or reject, and both conform. The schema leaves it optional so older entries stay readable; xdrcheck-corpus verify and the repository checks require it on every corpus entry.

flag.description: A bug class this input exercises (manifest.md section 9.5). Each expect.reject.reason has the flag of the same name in kebab case, and an entry with one carries that flag. core-lenient: stellar-core's own decoder accepts the input (core_behaviour.accepts).
